knownGaps: The contract clause is a clarification (V1.2), not a new freeze. It states an obligation the code already had to meet; it does not authorize any new DDL or data change.
The red cases cover the data-scope cluster only. They do not cover F1/F2/F3/F4/F5/F6, whose red cases arrive with their own waves (W2–W5).

F13's red case was added on a second pass: the first version of this wave only had middleware and permission tests, so RoleService.loadRoleDataScopes was covered by the acceptance probe but not by a unit test. It is now covered, but that gap existed for one iteration and is recorded rather than papered over.

The red run was produced by mutation, not by checking out the pre-W1 commit: the working tree carries a large amount of uncommitted tenant work from earlier sessions, so a commit-level revert was not available. The mutation reverts exactly the five predicates W1 introduced, and the checksums prove the tree was restored.

Nothing in this wave prevents a *new* predicate-free query from being written; the clause makes it reviewable and the tests guard the five known code points. A static check (lint for role_key queries without tenant_id) would be the real enforcement and is not part of this program.
